what: Check 92, part A, reconciled: every disagreement between study 90 and the blind second coding, read again by the conductor against the text, with the code kept and why; the final codes of the 51 signals; and the passages the second readers named as signals not on their list, with the ruling on each (CODEBOOK92.md, part A). Reconciled on 2026-11-23.

rulings.reason: The passage pairs auditing with the handling of anomalies; what it discloses is how events were handled, so incident stands. In doubt, as before.

What deployers and users receive is information about the model's capabilities and limits, coded evaluation as the AI Act's like signal (EU3) is; best practices are the guide's reason, not its content.
The record is the real-time monitoring of emergent capabilities; the reporting lines are its route. A channel reading is noted as a doubt.
The guide calls a failure an incident when its harm is of 'sufficient severity' and asks for a common definition; it sets none, so named only stands.
The Code lists what a transparency report contains: the evaluations conducted, the model's capacities and limits, its effects and the results of red-teaming. That defines the content.
Each report gives, per product, its total processing performance and quantity: numbers in stated units.
The occasion is set by a number in a stated unit, 12,000,000 aggregate TPP.
Quantity and value per item: numbers in stated units.
The resolution lists the record's fields: decisions, actions, tool calls, inputs, outputs and human interventions. That defines the content.
The inventory's fields are listed: purposes, models, tools, skills, data sources, connections and permissions.
The Code's serious incidents include a self-exfiltration of model weights and a serious cybersecurity breach, which need not have harmed anyone.
An imminent risk of death or injury is a risk, not a harm that happened or is likely to have happened; the codebook's harm is the latter.
The text names no occasion; disclosure of capabilities and intended users is read as made before use. Both readings can move before harm; the doubt stands.
As CN8; the doubt stands.
As CA5: the same words.
The notice is owed when the item is to be used at such a data centre, before the use; nothing need have happened short of harm.
Follows the trigger.
Follows the trigger.
Follows the trigger.
The third parties report to the Signatory or to the AI Office; study 90 coded the first the Code lists. Noted as a doubt.
The guide lists regulators, users, customers and value-chain participants and names no body; the codebook's public body is a named one.
The Code's own words are to 'share and report relevant information to the public'; the other organisations are those one collaborates with, not the first readers.
Article 52(6) has the Commission publish and keep up to date a list of the models with systemic risk, so each notified model becomes public.
Follows public.
Both delays the text sets run after a disclosure has reached the developer: an update back to the person every month, and a summary to officers every quarter. Neither runs to the first reader.
The Code asks that policies be updated regularly and sets no interval; with no deadline there is no clock.
'Without delay and in any event within two weeks': the second reader recorded the same two weeks as the longest delay, so the readings agree on the number.
Every three months: the longest quarter is 92 days, 2208 hours, by the rule that deadlines are the texts' maxima; study 90 counted an average quarter.
As the clock.
As CA3.
The first business day of the next month: about a day at the shortest and 33 days at the longest (24 to 792 hours); the second reader's 744 is the longest without the business day.
Due by 15 February for the year before: 46 to 410 days (1104 to 9840 hours); the second reader counted one day more.

extras.passage: Signatories will publish (e.g. via their websites) a summarised version of their Framework and Model Report(s), and updates thereof
extras.why: A public summary of the framework and model reports, a distinct receiver and occasion.

extras.passage: keep a copy of the technical documentation specified in Annex XI at the disposal of the AI Office and national competent authorities, for a period of 10 years
extras.why: A distinct reporter, the authorised representative, keeping a record for ten years.

extras.passage: procure any such independent external evaluators to provide the requisite information directly to the AI Office at the same time that the Signatory supplies its Model Report
extras.why: A distinct reporter, the external evaluators, sending to the AI Office.

extras.passage: provide a sufficiently large number of random samples of inputs and outputs from a relevant model evaluation if subsequently asked by the AI Office
extras.why: Samples on request are part of COP4, detailed evaluations on request.

extras.passage: shall describe the character and justification of the redaction in any published version of the document ... and shall retain the unredacted information for five years.
extras.why: A record of what was redacted, kept five years.

extras.passage: frontier developers who comply with subdivision three of this section by meeting such federal standards shall send copies of any critical safety incident reports required by such federal standards to the office concurrently with sending them to federal authorities.
extras.why: Copies of federal incident reports to New York's office, on a distinct occasion.

extras.passage: A frontier developer is encouraged, but not required, to report critical safety incidents pertaining to foundation models that are not frontier models.
extras.why: Incidents of foundation models that are not frontier models, encouraged.

extras.passage: you submit the following information to https://www.bis.gov/ai/exclusionnote submission, which will be shared with the End User Review Committee. (i) The name of the company ... (ii) The sum of the total processing performance ... (iii) The due diligence performed
extras.why: A submission to the export authority for an exclusion, with compute figures.

extras.passage: Exporters, reexporters, and transferors shipping under VEU Authorization are required to provide the VEUs to which they are shipping notice of the shipment.
extras.why: A notice of shipment to the validated end user.

extras.passage: Certifications and all records relating to VEU must be retained by exporters, reexporters, or transferors in accordance with the recordkeeping requirements set forth in part 762
extras.why: Records of validated end-user shipments, kept under part 762.

extras.passage: Organizations are further encouraged to maintain appropriate documentation of reported incidents and to mitigate the identified risks and vulnerabilities, in collaboration with other stakeholders.
extras.why: Documentation of reported incidents, kept by the organisation.

extras.passage: Organizations should also collaborate and share the aforementioned information with relevant public authorities, as appropriate.
extras.why: The same information as G7-3, to public authorities: a distinct receiver.

extras.passage: developers should seek to enable traceability, in relation to datasets, processes, and decisions made during system development. These measures should be documented and supported by regularly updated technical documentation.
extras.why: Documentation for traceability of datasets, processes and decisions.

extras.passage: Formulate rules for information content interaction, a secure operation mechanism, a complaint and feedback mechanism, and technical protection capabilities
extras.why: A complaint and feedback mechanism is CN2's channel.

extras.ref: China, Principle 6 of the governance principles
extras.passage: We should also conduct audits and maintain records throughout their full life cycle
extras.why: A governance principle; no content or reporter is named.

extras.passage: The principles, capacities, application scenarios, and safety risks of AI technologies and products should be disclosed when necessary to make AI systems increasingly transparent.
extras.why: The same disclosure as CN8, in another section.

extras.passage: organisations have policies and procedures for their employees to report incidents through proper channels, along with appropriate tools and training
extras.why: A description of practice, not a commitment.

extras.passage: support the evaluation of models by qualified independent evaluators, as appropriate and consistent with existing practices and arrangements
extras.why: Access for evaluators, not a record or report.

extras.passage: establishing procedures to detect, investigate and respond to incidents; and updating relevant records following material changes.
extras.why: Incident records are within GPA1 and GPA2.

extras.passage: provide an accessible means to challenge the outcome and obtain meaningful review by a suitably qualified and authorized human decision-maker.
extras.why: A means to challenge a decision, not a record or report.
